newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen slowing losses.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen slowing losses.

text.p: Polish shares fell in lower turnover in profit-taking on Wednesday after a three-session rise but analysts saw little potential for further losses and said the market should at least slow its falls on Thursday.

The main market's WIG index fell 344.6 points, or two percent, to 16,554.5, and turnover fell 7.7 percent to 202.3 million zlotys ($65 million) on all three markets as 80 issues fell, eight rose and eight were flat.
"The market isn't weak enough to experience deep falls, but on the other hand there is no leading power to push it up," said Tomasz Cwintal, an analyst at BGZ brokerage.

Analysts said the market was likely to extend its longer- term sideways drift as forthcoming summer holidays and September polls were cooling investor mood, while Poland's economy prospects prevented the bourse from deeper falls.
They said, falling inflation, economic growth and relative attractivness of many stocks was likely to keep the market above 16,000 points until the general elections.
Continuous trade amounted to 32.4 million zlotys ($10.5 million) with seven stocks closing lower, three higher, six flat and the WIG 20 index closing roughly flat at 1,640.9 points.
